recipes.name: Spicy Shrimp Creole
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds medium shrimp - peeled and deveined

steps.text: Heat oil in a Dutch oven on medium heat. Sauté celery, onions, and garlic in the Dutch oven until onions are pearly white and celery has begun to soften.

Mix sugar, flour, salt, pepper, and cayenne pepper into the Dutch oven. Add crushed tomatoes and tomato sauce, both pieces of bay leaf, and hot sauce. Bring mixture to a boil, then turn the heat to low.
Let mixture simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Approximately 15 minutes before serving, add shrimp to the pot and stir well. If necessary, raise the temperature to medium-low to ensure Creole is bubbling but not burning. Scoop out bay leaf halves before serving. Serve when shrimp is pink and thoroughly cooked.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Shrimp Creole
raw_recipe.description: This spicy shrimp Creole recipe combines shrimp with a variety of tasty spices that will create a dish that is sure to be a hit at your next party.

review.reviewBody: This is a quick and very good flavor. The only change I made was to 1/2 the recipe (just the two of us)and I used fresh tomotoes and fresh shrimp. Served with white rice, crusty bread and salad. Wonderful meal and very quick. I plan to use for a large family meal as it would be easy to pre-cook everything ahead. Just throw in the shrimp and reheat while preparing the rice. Nice company meal. Thanks for the post.

I am not at fan of very spicy food but wanted to try this version - but I did not use the cayenne pepper and I reduced the amount of hot sauce. However , I felt the recipe needed more oomph! Maybe that is why so much hot pepper seasoning was needed to give it the lift it needed. I was also surprised it did not use any green bell pepper . I added some Worcestershire sauce and 2 additional bay leaves ( left them whole). Simmered it longer to allow the flavors to meld. Then added the shrimp. Family enjoyed it!

First time making this, with a few changes. Sooooo delicious!!

Added bell peppers, a dash of worchester sauce, a teaspoon of green chile powder and substituted the cayenne pepper with red chile powder (a taste of New Mexico).

added chopped peppers, red and green with the onions. added 1/2 teaspoon of cumin,

served over Spanish rice,

I hate giving low ratings on recipes, but this one really disappointed. I should have been more leery when I saw the limited ingredients and the fact that they call for the shrimp to be cooked for 30 minutes- that’s over cooking by at least 20 minutes.
Added 1 T Cajun seasoning and reduced the cornstarch to 1 T. Also added crushed red pepper flakes. We like it spicy! My husband really liked it.

This was delicious and so easy! I left the shells on to add flavor to the sauce. They’re easy enough to pick off. I substituted tomato paste for the sauce and used chipotle chili with Texas Pete’s sauce.
I add a bell pepper, cooked the veggies with butter instead of oil and added 1 tblsp of worcestershire sauce to the mixture.

this recipe is good, it is some work though. i did use bell pepper instead of celery. and during the cooking process i added chicken broth, i cooked all day. and placed on jasimine rice. with garlic bread. the end result was very good, thanks, from florida

For starters, I halved the recipe. I added a green pepper, as well as 3 cloves of garlic instead of 2. I used red pepper instead of cayenne pepper because that was what I had on hand. I did not have hot sauce on hand, so I omitted that ingredient. I also used frozen shrimp instead of fresh. I put the meal in a dish and stuck it in the fridge overnight so the flavors could blend together. I reheated the creole the next night for dinner. I was so happy I omitted the hot sauce because it was almost too spicy for my taste! Next time, I will only put in 1/8 tsp red pepper. I served the creole with a Dole Light Caesar Salad Kit and french bread.

We added okra, cumin, oregano, thyme, extra garlic and substituted Emeril Lagasse's Creole seasoning combination and Sriracha Hot sauce for the other spices. Doubled the recommended amount of Shrimp. We served with a kale salad,broccoli garnish, homemade french bread and a dry french chardonnay. An excellent dining experience!

I used fresh tomatoes, added a 1/4 cup white wine, olive oil instead of vegetable oil. Turned out awesome, just the right amount of spice. Served it over parsley-butter rice to soften the heat a bit and roasted broccoli. Easily a crowd pleaser; can be made ahead of tim; I will be using in the future!
This is really good and really hot! My husband loved it as is, but I'm gonna have to back off on some of the spice next time so I can feel my tongue!!!!!
I downsized the recipe a bit, used crushed red pepper instead of cayenne and used corn starch for the flour. It's a shrimp creole that has really has a "kick" to it..really good.
simple and quick. I'll be making it often!

Reduced the portions to 4 as per the Allrecipes adjustment. Then made it as written. Delicious. Yes, spicy, but not too much so. Thought I would have left over but husband went back to the pan and ate the rest! [Note- I used cooked frozen shrimp that I defrosted in cold water for 15 minutes and then added to the sauce for maybe 5- 10 minutes.]
Plated it over rice, with broccolii.
Thank you for a yummy dinner!
I made it for a part of my family and they could not stop telling me how much they liked it. We tend to like spicy and this was spot on not too hot and not too mild!!
Very easy to prepare. I used cooked shrimp and put them in too early and they were a little over cooked. I won’t make the same mistake next time.
